paragraphs.text: On Sunday, Bill, Nick, and Michelle continued investigating the case.
This time, they met in Bill's room.
We have to find the Blackbeard and see who it belongs to.
I'm sure there's a connection between that boat and Mr. O'Nell.
There's a Naval Registry office at the port.
All boats at the port are listed there.
Good. Let's go to the port.
The Naval Registry was a small office near the Montego Yacht Club.
Michelle went in and talked to the clerk.
Hello. My name is Michelle Martin, and I need some information.
Said the clerk as he turned to his computer.
It's at Pier Number 8. That's where the biggest yachts are.
Can you tell me the name of the owner?
Let's see. It's Mr. Julian Devereaux from New Orleans.
Yes. Julian Devereaux. He and his wife are the owners of the New Wax Museum.
Said Michelle. She met Bill and Nick outside and told him about the Blackbeard.
So Julian and Gertrude Devereaux are the owners of the Wax Museum and the Blackbeard.
And they give a lot of money for the new park.
Why were they following the North Star at sea?
And what about the Wax Museum?
Why is Rover so attracted to it?
We know that the Blackbeard is at the port and that Julian Devereaux owns the boat and the Wax Museum.
There was a moment of silence.
The clerk said that Julian Devereaux is from New Orleans.
Let's go home and look on the web.
At home, they got on the web and found some interesting information.
Devereaux was the owner of a maritime museum in Charleston, South Carolina and a new art museum in Houston, Texas.
And guess what you find in museums?
Like the ones who now was looking for.
We have to find a way to get on the Blackbeard.
We could find some evidence of Devereaux's connection to this mystery.
The Blackbeard's at Pier Number Eight.
We can go one evening when the museum is open.
I don't want to meet them face to face.
The museum's always open on Friday and Saturday evenings until 10 p.m.
And the Devereaux are there on those evenings.
On Friday night Nick and I will try to get on the Blackbeard.
Michelle, you can sit in the coffee shop across the street from the museum.
If the Devereaux leave the building, call me on my cell phone.
It was November and almost Thanksgiving.
But the three friends could only think about the O'Nell case.
On Friday evening they met in front of the museum.
And Michelle ordered a cup of hot cocoa at the coffee shop.
She watched the museum entrance with her cell phone in her hand, ready to make a call.
There was no one at the port that evening.
The boys could hear their footsteps as they walked quickly past the North Star and turned left at Pier Number Eight.
The lights of the Blackbeard were on and the two boys stopped behind a van.
Let's wait here and see what happens.
Julian Devereaux got off the yacht and into his sports car and drove away.
They waited a few minutes and then got on the yacht.
The glass door was closed but not locked so it was easy to get in.
It was their first time on a yacht.
Drawers, cupboards, bookshelves, but they couldn't find anything.
Bill took a painting off the wall and turned it around but he found nothing.
He did the same with another painting and this time there was an envelope on the back.
Inside there was a map of the Florida coast and the Bermuda Triangle with some red pencil marks.
It was almost identical to the maps in Mr. O'Nell's house.
The Devaros have Mr. O'Nell's map and they hid it behind a painting.
Said Nick, staring at the map.
This is evidence that the Devaros are connected to Mr. O'Nell in some way.
We have to show this map to the police.
Bill put the empty envelope behind the painting.
Then he folded the map and put it in his shirt pocket.
They got back onto the pier and quickly left the port.
They picked up Michelle who was still at the coffee shop.
Let's go to Sandy's ice cream parlor and talk there.
